blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.11
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.11

blocks.text: प्रेक्षकाणीन्द्रियाणि
blocks.directed: [slowly] प्रेक्षकाणीन्द्रियाणि

blocks.text: Prekṣakāṇīndriyāṇi.
blocks.directed: Prekṣakāṇīndriyāṇi.

blocks.text: The senses are the spectators.
blocks.directed: The senses are the spectators.

blocks.text: Your Eyes Are Sitting in the Front Row Watching Śiva Perform.
blocks.directed: Your Eyes Are Sitting in the Front Row Watching Śiva Perform.

blocks.text: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN.
blocks.directed: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN.

blocks.text: WE HAVE A FULL THEATRE.
blocks.directed: WE HAVE A FULL THEATRE.

blocks.text: The Self is the dancer.
blocks.directed: The Self is the dancer.

blocks.text: The inner self is the stage.
blocks.directed: The inner self is the stage.

blocks.text: And the senses?
blocks.directed: And the senses?

blocks.text: The bloody audience.
blocks.directed: The bloody audience.

blocks.text: Now this is the sort of metaphor you could spend years contemplating.
blocks.directed: Now this is the sort of metaphor you could spend years contemplating.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it.

blocks.text: Prekṣaka — spectator, observer, someone who watches a performance.
blocks.directed: Prekṣaka — spectator, observer, someone who watches a performance.

blocks.text: Indriya — sense faculty.
blocks.directed: Indriya — sense faculty.

blocks.text: The plural forms give us:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The plural forms give us:

blocks.text: Prekṣakāṇi indriyāṇi.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Prekṣakāṇi indriyāṇi.

blocks.text: The senses are the spectators.
blocks.directed: The senses are the spectators.

blocks.text: Now, in ordinary life, we think of our senses primarily as channels for acquiring information about an external world.
blocks.directed: Now, in ordinary life, we think of our senses primarily as channels for acquiring information about an external world.

blocks.text: Eyes receive visual information.
blocks.directed: Eyes receive visual information.

blocks.text: Ears receive sound.
blocks.directed: Ears receive sound.

blocks.text: The skin responds to touch.
blocks.directed: The skin responds to touch.

blocks.text: And so on.
blocks.directed: And so on.

blocks.text: But in the Trika metaphysical system, the senses are powers of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But in the Trika metaphysical system, the senses are powers of consciousness.

blocks.text: They’re not ultimately independent entities capable of knowing without the conscious reality through which experience occurs.
blocks.directed: They’re not ultimately independent entities capable of knowing without the conscious reality through which experience occurs.

blocks.text: And here’s where Kṣemarāja makes an absolutely beautiful move.
blocks.directed: And here’s where Kṣemarāja makes an absolutely beautiful move.

blocks.text: The senses, ordinarily directed outward towards their objects, are described as becoming inwardly aware of their own essential nature.
blocks.directed: The senses, ordinarily directed outward towards their objects, are described as becoming inwardly aware of their own essential nature.

blocks.text: And this inward recognition is associated with camatkāra.
blocks.directed: And this inward recognition is associated with camatkāra.

blocks.text: Astonishment.
blocks.directed: Astonishment.

blocks.text: Wonder.
blocks.directed: Wonder.

blocks.text: Aesthetic delight.
blocks.directed: Aesthetic delight.

blocks.text: The extraordinary savour of consciousness recognising itself.
blocks.directed: The extraordinary savour of consciousness recognising itself.

blocks.text: Now, you might remember this from the first book.
blocks.directed: Now, you might remember this from the first book.

blocks.text: विस्मयो योगभूमिकाः।
blocks.directed: [slowly] विस्मयो योगभूमिकाः।

blocks.text: Vismayo yogabhūmikāḥ.
blocks.directed: Vismayo yogabhūmikāḥ.

blocks.text: The stages of yoga are wonder.
blocks.directed: The stages of yoga are wonder.

blocks.text: And now the same aesthetic dimension returns through the theatre metaphor.
blocks.directed: And now the same aesthetic dimension returns through the theatre metaphor.

blocks.text: The universe is a performance.
blocks.directed: The universe is a performance.

blocks.text: The Self is the actor.
blocks.directed: The Self is the actor.

blocks.text: The senses are the spectators.
blocks.directed: The senses are the spectators.

blocks.text: And the experience of recognition becomes a kind of supreme aesthetic delight.
blocks.directed: And the experience of recognition becomes a kind of supreme aesthetic delight.

blocks.text: This is where Trika’s philosophy connects beautifully with the wider Kashmiri tradition of aesthetics.
blocks.directed: This is where Trika’s philosophy connects beautifully with the wider Kashmiri tradition of aesthetics.

blocks.text: Think about watching a magnificent play.
blocks.directed: Think about watching a magnificent play.

blocks.text: For a moment, you’re completely absorbed.
blocks.directed: For a moment, you’re completely absorbed.

blocks.text: The performance draws you in.
blocks.directed: The performance draws you in.

blocks.text: The characters, emotions, movement, music and atmosphere form an extraordinary unity.
blocks.directed: The characters, emotions, movement, music and atmosphere form an extraordinary unity.

blocks.text: You experience something beyond simply processing individual bits of sensory information.
blocks.directed: You experience something beyond simply processing individual bits of sensory information.

blocks.text: There’s a distinctive delight in the manifestation itself.
blocks.directed: There’s a distinctive delight in the manifestation itself.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja uses the concept of camatkāra to describe the heightened experience of the yogi whose senses become established in recognition.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja uses the concept of camatkāra to describe the heightened experience of the yogi whose senses become established in recognition.

blocks.text: But the metaphysical claim goes further than ordinary aesthetic appreciation.
blocks.directed: But the metaphysical claim goes further than ordinary aesthetic appreciation.

blocks.text: In an ordinary performance, the spectator remains distinct from the actor.
blocks.directed: In an ordinary performance, the spectator remains distinct from the actor.

blocks.text: Here, the senses themselves are powers of the same Self that performs the drama.
blocks.directed: Here, the senses themselves are powers of the same Self that performs the drama.

blocks.text: So the separation between actor and spectators is not ultimate.
blocks.directed: So the separation between actor and spectators is not ultimate.

blocks.text: The conscious reality is the source of both.
blocks.directed: The conscious reality is the source of both.

blocks.text: And now comes a rather extraordinary consequence.
blocks.directed: And now comes a rather extraordinary consequence.

blocks.text: The senses no longer have to function exclusively as sources of distraction.
blocks.directed: The senses no longer have to function exclusively as sources of distraction.

blocks.text: Seeing can become an occasion for recognition.
blocks.directed: Seeing can become an occasion for recognition.

blocks.text: Hearing can become an occasion for recognition.
blocks.directed: Hearing can become an occasion for recognition.

blocks.text: The appearance of a sensation can become an occasion for recognition.
blocks.directed: The appearance of a sensation can become an occasion for recognition.

blocks.text: Because the senses themselves are not outside Śiva.
blocks.directed: Because the senses themselves are not outside Śiva.

blocks.text: Their capacity to disclose manifestation belongs to Śakti.
blocks.directed: Their capacity to disclose manifestation belongs to Śakti.

blocks.text: And this is a major difference between simply suppressing sensory experience and recognising its conscious source.
blocks.directed: And this is a major difference between simply suppressing sensory experience and recognising its conscious source.

blocks.text: The point isn’t:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The point isn’t:

blocks.text: “Never look at anything.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Never look at anything.”

blocks.text: “Never listen to anything.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Never listen to anything.”

blocks.text: “Never enjoy anything.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Never enjoy anything.”

blocks.text: It’s more subtle.
blocks.directed: It’s more subtle.

blocks.text: Don’t mistake the objects disclosed by the senses for realities ultimately independent of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Don’t mistake the objects disclosed by the senses for realities ultimately independent of consciousness.

blocks.text: And don’t mistake the sensory faculties themselves for autonomous sources of awareness.
blocks.directed: And don’t mistake the sensory faculties themselves for autonomous sources of awareness.

blocks.text: Recognise the conscious reality through which the entire sensory drama becomes manifest.
blocks.directed: Recognise the conscious reality through which the entire sensory drama becomes manifest.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explicitly invokes the Kaṭha Upaniṣad in explaining the inward turn of the senses.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explicitly invokes the Kaṭha Upaniṣad in explaining the inward turn of the senses.

blocks.text: The ordinary direction of attention is outward.
blocks.directed: The ordinary direction of attention is outward.

blocks.text: But the wise seeker turns inward towards the Self.
blocks.directed: But the wise seeker turns inward towards the Self.

blocks.text: And in the context of this sūtra, the result is the delightful recognition of the conscious actor through the senses themselves. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: And in the context of this sūtra, the result is the delightful recognition of the conscious actor through the senses themselves. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now imagine standing in a busy marketplace.
blocks.directed: Now imagine standing in a busy marketplace.

blocks.text: People moving.
blocks.directed: People moving.

blocks.text: Voices overlapping.
blocks.directed: Voices overlapping.

blocks.text: Colours appearing.
blocks.directed: Colours appearing.

blocks.text: Smells rising from food stalls.
blocks.directed: Smells rising from food stalls.

blocks.text: A tremendous sensory performance.
blocks.directed: A tremendous sensory performance.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, attention is scattered among its objects.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, attention is scattered among its objects.

blocks.text: But in the contemplative interpretation, the practitioner begins recognising the underlying conscious reality through which all these perceptions appear.
blocks.directed: But in the contemplative interpretation, the practitioner begins recognising the underlying conscious reality through which all these perceptions appear.

blocks.text: The sights and sounds don’t necessarily have to stop.
blocks.directed: The sights and sounds don’t necessarily have to stop.

blocks.text: The theatre continues.
blocks.directed: The theatre continues.

blocks.text: But the spectators discover the true nature of the actor.
blocks.directed: But the spectators discover the true nature of the actor.

blocks.text: And this is why the three sūtras belong together.
blocks.directed: And this is why the three sūtras belong together.

blocks.text: नर्तक आत्मा।
blocks.directed: [slowly] नर्तक आत्मा।

blocks.text: The Self is the dancer.
blocks.directed: The Self is the dancer.

blocks.text: रङ्गोऽन्तरात्मा।
blocks.directed: [slowly] रङ्गोऽन्तरात्मा।

blocks.text: The inner self is the stage.
blocks.directed: The inner self is the stage.

blocks.text: प्रेक्षकाणीन्द्रियाणि।
blocks.directed: [slowly] प्रेक्षकाणीन्द्रियाणि।

blocks.text: The senses are the spectators.
blocks.directed: The senses are the spectators.

blocks.text: What an extraordinary little metaphysical trilogy.
blocks.directed: What an extraordinary little metaphysical trilogy.

blocks.text: The universe is a drama of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The universe is a drama of consciousness.

blocks.text: And the yogi, through recognition, discovers the conscious unity underlying the entire performance.
blocks.directed: And the yogi, through recognition, discovers the conscious unity underlying the entire performance.

blocks.text: Now, the obvious question is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Now, the obvious question is:

blocks.text: How does this recognition become stable?
blocks.directed: How does this recognition become stable?

blocks.text: Because it’s all very well understanding the theatre metaphor.
blocks.directed: Because it’s all very well understanding the theatre metaphor.

blocks.text: But you can intellectually appreciate the idea that consciousness is the actor and still spend your entire life absolutely furious about the plot.
blocks.directed: But you can intellectually appreciate the idea that consciousness is the actor and still spend your entire life absolutely furious about the plot.

blocks.text: So Vasugupta moves to the next question.
blocks.directed: So Vasugupta moves to the next question.

blocks.text: What enables the yogi to recognise the subtle conscious reality underlying the performance?
blocks.directed: What enables the yogi to recognise the subtle conscious reality underlying the performance?

blocks.text: The answer involves a rather important form of intelligence.
blocks.directed: The answer involves a rather important form of intelligence.
